ahead: hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_CROSS_TERM_CANCELLATION.md proves, for PRIME q only, an exact identity Sigma_cross(q) = Sigma_diag(q)/(q-1) - E(q) (E(q)>=0, E(q)~T_N), verified to floating-point precision (worst rel err 3.4e-11) across q in {3,5,7,11,13,17,19}, N up to 1e6. This upgrades RANK3_ROUTE_D.md (D8)'s ceiling phi(q)^2*sum_b T(q,b) to q*sum_b T(q,b) for prime q, landing exactly on the 'diagonal-only' weight mu(q)^2/phi(q) that RANK3_ROUTE_D.md Section 5 left undetermined -- one full power of phi(q) saved, via genuine Dirichlet-character-orthogonality + Gauss-sum-twisting cancellation, not an assumption. It does NOT reach RANK3_POLYRANGE.md's guessed weight mu(q)^2/phi(q)^2 (a second power), and nothing found here suggests that second power is available by this method. For COMPOSITE SQUAREFREE q (tested q in {6,10,15}), the same identity applied naively is wrong by 50-156% (not floating-point noise): the proof's one primality-dependent step -- every nonprincipal character mod q is primitive -- is false for composite squarefree q, so the off-diagonal Gauss-sum matrix G(chi,chi') need not vanish. This document does not evaluate G(chi,chi') for imprimitive characters (the classical reduction of an imprimitive character's twisted sum to the primitive character inducing it, a formula involving mu(q/q*) with q* the conductor, was identified but not carried out). Consequence for the overall rank-3 q-sum: restricted to prime q alone, partial summation (reusing RANK3_POLYRANGE_TINT_CHECK.md Section 3's method) gives O_eps(N^{2+eps}) for that sub-sum -- but composite squarefree q (the majority of squarefree integers by density) remain at the unimproved O(1) weight, so the FULL 2<=q<=R_0 sum's order is UNCHANGED at O(N^{5/2}) (matching, not beating, CHHL) unless composite q are separately handled. This is additional to, and independent of, RANK3_ROUTE_D.md Section 6's separate transfer-step obstruction (already found costing O(N^3) when summed naively over q) and RANK3_SCOPE.md Route A's Delta(t;q,b)-uniformity requirement -- neither of those is touched by this document.

work.what: In hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_ROUTE_D.md's exact identity (D7), Sigma_cross(q) = sum_{b != b' mod q}^* c_q(b-b') X(b,b') (b,b' ranging over reduced residues mod q, c_q the Ramanujan sum, X(b,b') = <K_N D_b, K_N D_b'>_{L^2(T)} the Gram-matrix cross term defined in that document's (D6)). hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_CROSS_TERM_CANCELLATION.md proves, for q PRIME, the exact identity Sigma_cross(q) = Sigma_diag(q)/(q-1) - E(q), where Sigma_diag(q) = phi(q) sum_{b mod q}^* T(q,b) (T(q,b) = X(b,b), that document's (D5)), and E(q) = sum_{t=1}^N Delta_eps(t;q)^2 + sum_{t=1}^{N-1} [Delta_eps(N;q) - Delta_eps(t;q)]^2 with Delta_eps(t;q) = psi_cop(t;q) - t, psi_cop(t;q) = sum_{n<=t, gcd(n,q)=1} Lambda(n) (Lambda the von Mangoldt function). The proof goes via the classical Dirichlet-character orthogonality relation 1_{n = b mod q} = (1/phi(q)) sum_{chi mod q} chibar(b) chi(n) for (n,q)=1, applied to decompose D_b(beta) = S_b(beta) - K_N(beta)/phi(q) (S_b(beta) = sum_{n<=N, n=b mod q} Lambda(n) e(n beta), K_N(beta) = sum_{n=1}^N e(n beta)) into a principal-character piece and a sum over nonprincipal characters, then summing over the reduced residues a mod q using c_q(a) = mu(q) (valid for every q) and the classical Gauss-sum twist tau_a(chibar) := sum_{b mod q}^* chibar(b) e(ab/q) = chi(a) tau(chibar) with |tau(chibar)|^2 = q -- an identity that holds ONLY when chi is a PRIMITIVE character mod q. For q PRIME every nonprincipal character mod q is automatically primitive (the only proper divisor of q is 1), which is exactly what makes the proof go through. The task: extend this to composite SQUAREFREE q (q with >= 2 distinct prime factors, still mu(q)^2 != 0), where some nonprincipal characters mod q are IMPRIMITIVE (induced by a character mod a proper divisor q* | q, q* < q -- e.g. for q=6, phi(6)=2, the single nonprincipal character mod 6 is induced by the Legendre symbol mod 3, and there is no primitive nonprincipal character mod 6 at all). For imprimitive chi, the twist sum tau_a(chibar) = sum_{b mod q}^* chibar(b) e(ab/q) does NOT equal chi(a) tau(chibar) in general, and |tau(chibar)| != sqrt(q) in general; the classical reduction expresses an imprimitive character's Gauss-type sum in terms of the PRIMITIVE character chi* mod q* that induces it, via a formula involving mu(q/q*) (see e.g. Apostol, Introduction to Analytic Number Theory, or Montgomery-Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, the sections on imprimitive characters and induced moduli -- this repository's own worktree may or may not have these sources locally; RANK3_POLYRANGE_TINT_CHECK.md in this same hunt already recorded that WebSearch/WebFetch were denied in its worktree, so check for local access before assuming a live literature search is available). Compute G(chi,chi') := sum_{a mod q}^* tau_a(chibar) * conj(tau_a(chibar')) for EVERY pair of nonprincipal characters chi, chi' mod q (not just primitive ones), using this induced-character reduction, and determine whether G(chi,chi') is small off the diagonal (chi != chi') the way it is exactly zero for prime q, or genuinely large. If it can be shown small (even with worse constants than the prime case), redo the derivation in hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_CROSS_TERM_CANCELLATION.md Section 3 for composite squarefree q using this G(chi,chi') to get an analogous bound on Sigma_diag(q) + Sigma_cross(q) (ideally still O(q) * sum_b^* T(q,b), or state precisely what weight is reachable and why it differs from the prime case). Verify any resulting exact identity numerically to floating-point precision (not just approximately) against the existing ground-truth machinery in hunts/prime_pair_error/rank3_cross_term_probe.py (import and reuse its reduced_residues, delta_table, T_and_X, ramanujan_sum_direct functions -- do not reimplement Sigma_diag/Sigma_cross/T(q,b) from scratch) at q in {6, 10, 14, 15, 21} (squarefree composites already in or near this hunt's existing moduli ladders) and N up to at least 10^6, the same way hunts/prime_pair_error/rank3_cross_term_cancellation_probe.py already does for prime q. If no clean extension is found after genuinely attempting the induced-character reduction, state precisely and specifically what breaks (not just 'it's hard') and what would be needed instead -- that is itself a valid, useful outcome for this task, as several sibling documents in this hunt (e.g. RANK3_POLYRANGE_TINT_CHECK.md Section 2, RANK3_ROUTE_D.md Section 7) already do for other sub-problems. hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_CROSS_TERM_CANCELLATION.md Section 5 states, but does not carry out in full arithmetic detail with explicit constants, that restricting the sum sum_{q=2}^{R_0} mu(q)^2/phi(q) sum_{a mod q}^* integral_1^N (psi(t;q,a) - t/phi(q))^2 dt (R_0 = floor(sqrt(N)/3)/log(N), the exact range this hunt calls rank 3 -- see hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_SCOPE.md) to PRIME q only gives O_eps(N^{2+eps}), by the same classical-Barban-Davenport-Halberstam-plus-Abel-summation method that hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_POLYRANGE_TINT_CHECK.md Section 3 already carries out in full for the weight mu(q)^2/phi(q)^2 over ALL squarefree q <= R_0 (not just primes). Task: write out that argument in full for the PRIME-only sum with weight mu(q)^2/phi(q) ~ 1/q (reuse RANK3_POLYRANGE_TINT_CHECK.md Section 3's structure: define f(q) = sum_a^* sum_t Delta(t;q,a)^2, F(Q) = sum_{q prime, q<=Q} f(q), bound F(Q) using classical (BDH) restricted to a sum over primes q<=Q only (BDH's own bound D(t,Q) << Qt log t covers sum over ALL q<=Q, and a sum restricted to primes is trivially bounded by the same quantity since f(q)>=0, so F(Q) << Q N^2 log N still holds for the prime-restricted F; state this reduction explicitly rather than assuming it), then Abel-sum against w(q) = mu(q)^2/phi(q) restricted to primes (w(q) = 1/(q-1) exactly at primes) to get the final N^{2+eps} bound with an explicit exponent of log N, matching the style of RANK3_POLYRANGE_TINT_CHECK.md's boxed result. This closes out, with full rigor and an explicit statement, the one part of RANK3_CROSS_TERM_CANCELLATION.md Section 5's claim that was asserted by analogy rather than derived in full.
